---
title: "Inside a project folder"
subtitle: "What every file and directory in a Flux project is, and which ones are yours"
---

A Flux project is a plain folder whose marker is `project.json`. Here is the canonical tree:

```
<project>/
├── project.json                 # the map: title, authors, documents, figures, references
├── paper/                       # YOURS — documents and arbitrary nested folders
│   ├── notes.qmd                #   a starter document; no required main.qmd
│   ├── notes.comments.json      #   its margin-comment threads
│   └── _quarto.yml              #   shared export settings
├── plots/                       # YOURS — analysis output lands here, any structure you like
│   ├── growth.{svg,fluxplot.json,recipe.json}   # a semantic plot + manifest + recipe
│   ├── _dissections/growth/     #   growth's companion material (per-subject panels, stats CSVs)
│   ├── _lighttable/             #   Lighttable collections for exploratory image sets
│   ├── pasted/                  #   originals of images pasted from the clipboard
│   └── paper_snips/             #   regions snipped out of PDFs in the reader
├── fig/                         # APP-MANAGED — the figure subsystem
│   ├── index.json               #   canvases + figures rollup
│   ├── canvases/<id>.json       #   the real compositions (figures → elements)
│   ├── captions/<id>.md         #   composed caption mirror, reconciled with the composition
│   ├── assets/                  #   accepted plot bundles (SVG + semantic sidecars)
│   └── renders/                 #   derived static renders
├── slides/<deckId>/deck.json    # APP-MANAGED — one deck per folder (+ its assets/)
├── references/library.bib       # YOURS — the project's cited subset (BibTeX)
├── Context/                     # the agent layer
│   ├── Project/MISSION.qmd      #   the charter (co-owned: you have final say)
│   ├── NOTEBOOK.md              #   the principal agent's running memory
│   ├── RULES.md                 #   project rules (recurring feedback lands here)
│   ├── Transcripts/             #   captured agent-session transcripts
│   └── Dispatches/              #   worker briefs, logs, and results
├── styles/  assets/  exports/   # figure styles · media · compiled output (derived)
└── .meta/                       # tool state: journal, feedback ledger, locks, schemas
```

# Ownership at a glance

| Kind | Paths | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Yours — edit freely** | `paper/**.qmd` (legacy: `manuscript/`), `plots/`, `references/library.bib` | Source of truth. Edit in Flux, another editor, or a script — all equivalent. |
| **Co-owned with agents** | `Context/` | Mission and rules are shared; `NOTEBOOK.md` is the agent's memory — read and comment rather than rewrite. |
| **App-managed** | `fig/`, `slides/` | Readable JSON, but change it through the app or [`flux` commands](cli.qmd) so indexes and captions stay coherent. |
| **Derived** | `fig/renders/`, `exports/`, caches | Rebuildable output. Safe to ignore in backups and version control. |

# Notes on specific pieces

- **`project.json`** is a derived rollup — a fast map of the project, rebuilt from the real
  files (`flux reindex` refreshes it if a script edited things directly).
- **Figure identity lives in the composition.** A permanent `referenceKey` survives title,
  number, and canvas changes; `index.json` and project rollups preserve it when rebuilt.
  Filenames use persistent IDs. Paper document order has no effect on those identities.
  Caption markdown is a readable mirror: independent edits reconcile against the last saved
  version, while conflicting edits are preserved and reported instead of silently replacing
  one another. `.meta/figure-reference-update.json`, when present, protects an interrupted
  panel-reference rewrite until recovery finishes.
- **Comments live beside documents, never in them.** New documents use
  `<name>.comments.json`. A legacy main manuscript retains its historical `comments.json`.
  Moving a document in Paper moves its comments too.
- **Older layouts remain supported.** `manuscript/` is discovered alongside `paper/`; Flux
  never renames an existing project folder automatically. New manifests name `documentRoot`
  as `paper` and retain `manuscript.path` as a default export pointer for compatibility.
  That pointer may be empty when all ordinary documents have been deleted.
- **`plots/` is a drop-zone with no imposed structure** — organize it however your analysis
  does. Flux only reads it, copying what you compose into `fig/assets/`. See
  [semantic plots](../concepts/semantic-plots.qmd) for the three-file contract. Two
  subfolders are written *for* you, and are yours to keep or delete: `plots/pasted/` holds
  the original of every image you paste from the clipboard, and `plots/paper_snips/` holds
  every region you snip out of a PDF. Both exist so the pixels you contribute live somewhere
  you own, not only inside the app's `fig/assets/` copy. Two names are reserved, both starting
  with `_`: `plots/_dissections/` holds each plot's
  [companion material](../concepts/dissections.qmd) (the **D** key in the figure editor views
  it), and `plots/_lighttable/` is where [Lighttable](../lighttable.qmd) collections belong —
  the sweeps and per-cell batches you triage before choosing a panel. Neither shows up in an
  ordinary plot-importer search, however many thousands of images they hold; type **`_`** in
  the importer to list them and **Enter** to search inside one.
- **`.meta/`** holds the operational machinery: `journal.ndjson` (every write: who/what/when),
  `feedback.ndjson` (your context-stamped notes to agents), advisory `locks/`, JSON `schema/`
  for every file type, and the live-bridge descriptor while the app is open.
- **`Context/`** is explained in full in [the collaboration system](../agents/collaboration.qmd).

For the philosophy behind the layout — source vs. derived, crash safety, live reload —
see [Projects are folders, files are the truth](../concepts/projects-and-files.qmd).
